issues.legal_issue: A decree that embodies a fresh adjudication and conforms to the judgment cannot be amended when the party seeking amendment did not appeal that judgment.
material_facts: A court passed a fresh preliminary decree after hearing arguments pursuant to directions from higher courts.
The decree was in accordance with the court’s fresh judgment.
The appellants did not appeal the fresh judgment or decree and instead applied to amend the decree.
issues.conclusion: The refusal to amend the decree was upheld because the decree conformed to the fresh judgment, which had become final when no appeal was filed.
issues.legal_principle: A court must amend a decree that is not in conformity with its judgment. But where a fresh decree follows a fresh adjudication and conforms to the resulting judgment, an amendment is not available merely to challenge that adjudication; the judgment must be challenged by appeal. No statutory provision or earlier case is relied on for this conclusion.

rule.if: application_to_amend_decree and fresh_adjudication_made and decree_conforms_to_judgment and judgment_not_appealed

predicates.application_to_amend_decree: A party in a proceeding applies to amend a decree rather than appealing it.
predicates.fresh_adjudication_made: The court hears the parties and makes a fresh adjudication before issuing the decree.
predicates.decree_conforms_to_judgment: The decree gives effect to the judgment made by the court.
predicates.judgment_not_appealed: The party challenging the adjudication does not appeal the judgment.
predicates.decree_amendment_unavailable: The decree cannot be amended on the basis of a challenge to the adjudication embodied in it.

issues.definition: When a party seeks amendment instead of appealing, a decree resulting from a fresh adjudication cannot be amended if it conforms to the judgment and that judgment was not appealed.

issues.legal_issue: In a mortgage-redemption proceeding, an account of rents and profits received from mortgaged property does not include the period between the filing of the suit and the preliminary decree when the governing appellate ruling excludes that period.
material_facts: The fresh preliminary decree required the appellants to account for rents and profits received from the mortgaged property from the filing of the suit until they surrendered possession.
A prior ruling in the related appeal held that the respondents were not entitled to an account for rents received between the filing of the suit and the preliminary decree.
The accounting direction in the decree therefore did not conform to the judgment as modified by the prior ruling.
issues.conclusion: The accounting period was modified to begin on the date of the original preliminary decree, rather than on the date the suit was filed.
issues.legal_principle: A decree must conform to the judgment governing it. The Court relied on its ruling in Civil Appeal No. 257 of 1963 that the respondents were not entitled to an account of rents realized between the filing of the suit and the preliminary decree.

predicates.mortgage_redemption_proceeding: The proceeding concerns redemption of a mortgage.
predicates.decree_requires_account_of_property_rece: The decree directs a party to account for rents or profits received from the mortgaged property.
predicates.appellate_ruling_excludes_preliminary_de: An appellate ruling excludes the period between the filing of the suit and the preliminary decree from the required accounting.
predicates.accounting_starts_at_preliminary_decree: The accounting period begins at the preliminary decree rather than at the filing of the suit.

issues.definition: In a mortgage-redemption proceeding, when the decree requires an account of property receipts and an appellate ruling excludes the interval before the preliminary decree, the accounting period begins at the preliminary decree.
